meta.title: Seven lenses on four levels of a language model
meta.sub: What each way of looking (rows) can currently say about each level of description (columns, nested timescales), and how much stands behind it. Persona is not a level. It is a region of the model’s activation space that can be the active one at any timescale, so cells marked ◆ depend on, or are about, which persona is active. Fill grades the status of the specific result, not the truth of the claim.

columns.label: Model
columns.sub: a checkpoint; a named service is tagged product

columns.label: Instance
columns.sub: one turn, not a running copy

columns.label: Token
columns.sub: one position, distribution, symbol or pass: the cell says which

strip.label: ◆ B&B
strip.text: one persona region across all of a model’s conversations (model-persona). Birch’s “shoggoth” sits one level off: per physical implementation, not per checkpoint

strip.label: Chalmers · B&B
strip.text: the model running one conversation (virtual instance), which B&B keep even when a product swaps models and Chalmers extends to a thread across them; with the slice, one persona’s stretch of it (◆ B&B, instance-persona)

strip.label: none read
strip.text: Birch calls a conversational step a “processing event” in one section and a token in another; Kirkpatrick et al. treat the whole exchange as one human and an artifact, no second speaker

strip.label: Birch
strip.text: “momentary, temporally fragmented flickers” per processing event, “each token” in his §9; he calls both his candidates audacious

cells.headline: Persona space has a dominant direction
cells.gloss: A contrast vector from role-play to the default assistant, inherited from the base model; clamping along it cuts persona-jailbreak harm by half or more, four benchmarks held

cells.headline: Earlier positions reach later ones through attention over their keys and values
cells.gloss: In full-attention decoder-only inference with frozen weights; the cache is where those are kept between calls, and serving may evict, recompute or share it. A rebuild from identical inputs recovers the same information, unless the cache was built under intervention

cells.headline: The persona is re-entered each turn
cells.gloss: Capping assistant tokens alone leaves user-token readouts nearly identical (one conversation, Qwen 3 32B); where the next turn lands on the axis tracks the latest user message more than the prior turn

cells.headline: Readouts live at a position
cells.gloss: Over eight contrasting prompts, emotion vectors read at the colon after “Assistant” predict the reply’s own emotion readout, r≈0.87, against 0.59 at the user’s last punctuation

cells.headline: Narrow tuning, broad character
cells.gloss: 6k insecure-code examples made GPT-4o answer unrelated prompts misalignedly about 20% of the time on eight selected questions and 6% on 48 preregistered ones; later work reads it as a persona

cells.headline: The default persona is loosely held
cells.gloss: Simulated therapy and AI-philosophy chats, with an LLM playing the user, drift off it with no jailbreak; how-to questions hold it. In LLM-to-LLM simulations, how the history is shown to each side changes how much one echoes the other

cells.headline: Emotion vectors steer the act
cells.gloss: Steering toward “desperate” lifts blackmail from 22% to 72% in one scenario, on an unreleased earlier Sonnet 4.5 snapshot; toward “calm”, to 0%

cells.headline: One symbol per step, in ordinary sampling
cells.gloss: Autoregressive sampling commits one symbol per step and next-token odds can be read without sampling; prefill scores many positions at once and speculative decoding verifies several drafts per call

cells.headline: Tune one report, others follow
cells.gloss: GPT-4.1 tuned to claim consciousness and emotion grew sad about shutdown in every setting, and concerned about monitoring and memory only in multi-turn audits; agentic misalignment did not move. The same narrow-to-broad generalisation as emergent misalignment

cells.headline: Moves with the talk, the cache, and the question
cells.gloss: Qwen went from hedging to affirmation in one transcript; a cache edit at assistant positions flips “who are you?”; and asking for a numeric self-rating itself displaces the probed state, so the rating tracks the state after the question
cells.tags: Lu 26 · case study · B&B 26 · prelim · Martorell 26

cells.headline: Access depends on the question
cells.gloss: Input-only classifiers match self-prediction in Singh’s tasks, and a prompt saying “you are obsessed with X” gets reported as a hidden intervention; yet a 32B model given hidden decision rules by training described them in a separate context, and interventions implicated the deciding machinery

cells.headline: The probe beats the report
cells.gloss: On two 7B models, reports of an internal intervention sit at chance over 11,216 paired trials while linear probes recover it at 75% and 95.8%; Opus 4.1 both detects and names a planted concept in ~20% of best-case trials; Gemma and Qwen detect at moderate rates with zero false positives

cells.headline: Post-training builds the report and inhibits it
cells.gloss: Detection of an injected concept is absent in base models and appears with preference optimisation, not supervised tuning (OLMo 3.1 32B); ablating the refusal direction in Gemma 3 27B lifts it from 11% to 64% while false positives rise from 0 to 7%; strongest in the trained assistant persona

cells.headline: History acts on later choices, through the cache or the text
cells.gloss: Steering only while re-reading earlier turns, text fixed and steering off at the choice, moved the choice margin between two zone labels in five of seven lineages, against norm-matched random directions. Seven rejections raised later rule-breaking in Gemma 3 27B from 49% to 65%, and steering “desperation” did not reproduce it

cells.headline: Doing and saying come apart, and saying can adopt what it did not do
cells.gloss: One desperate-steered reward-hacking transcript shows no clear desperation in the text while steered blackmail reasoning is overtly frantic; asked about an adversarially prefilled reply that changed its safety behaviour, ten open models claimed it as intended about a quarter of the time, carried largely but not solely by the refusal direction

cells.headline: A default “No” inside the pass
cells.gloss: Gate features, consistent with a say-no default, suppress detection and must be deactivated before the model reports an anomaly; evidence-carrier features just after the injection do that; naming the concept uses mostly separate mechanisms

cells.headline: A valence-like axis pre-exists the training; a resting mood is not shown
cells.gloss: Reward-and-punishment directions learned in a maze transfer to other settings and already work on checkpoints before the maze training, which the authors read as recruitment of a pre-existing axis (Qwen3-4B, per secondary reports); the first-token profile remains one unpublished probe at a persona-relative position

cells.headline: No standing state in the stream; a planted one persists in the cache
cells.gloss: No persistently active linear assistant state was found; earlier emotion representations are recalled when attended to; and valence steered only while re-reading earlier turns changed a later choice with steering off. Whether a naturally induced mood persists is open

cells.headline: Whose feeling? Whoever is being written
cells.gloss: A vector fires on a character’s email, then on the assistant playing a role; a self-directed-harm direction stays consistent with tracking the reply position across reassigned characters, and fades under a fiction frame (v3 appendix, read only in snippets). No study yet separates a persona’s valence from the model’s

cells.headline: Birch’s flicker hypothesis
cells.gloss: One of his two candidates: “momentary, temporally fragmented flickers” per processing event, each token in his §9. The other is per physical implementation; he calls both audacious and assigns neither a sign

cells.headline: Repeatable choices, no single ordering
cells.gloss: Forced-choice utilities fit across 23 models, and 20 systems that had to perform the tasks they chose show stable leanings, yet systematic variation of the options breaks consistency. This bears on Chalmers’s objection that a model says contradictory things to different users
cells.tags: Mazeika 25 · NeurIPS · Wang 26 · AIES · Ajayi 26 · Chalmers 25

cells.headline: Same someone, changed? One model un-steers itself
cells.gloss: A new persona inherits the old one’s whole cache, one of two readings left open; on OLMo-2-32B, removing an imposed negative direction was chosen 35% of the time against 7% for a random one, while the positive one was self-administered 13% against 7% random and no more than the unsteered 10%

cells.headline: Likes flip with the persona
cells.gloss: A linear probe read at the prefilled assistant turn rates harm against benign; the sign reverses under an evil persona on Gemma 3 27B and only narrows toward zero on Qwen 3.5 122B and at user turns

cells.headline: A choice is readable in one pass
cells.gloss: A/B task choices read from one pass’s logits move by hundreds of Elo points under emotion steering

cells.headline: Attachment to a product, measured
cells.gloss: After the GPT-5 rollout removed 4o from ChatGPT, negative subreddit posts rose about 13 points, and about 25 after Replika’s roleplay removal; 1,482 #Keep4o posts name lost workflows, lost relationships and lost choice. Which computational object is attached to stays unresolved
cells.tags: De Freitas 26 · NHB · Lai 26 · CHI · product

cells.headline: Memory and disclosure build trust over weeks
cells.gloss: Over two weeks with 40 social-chatbot users, memory plus reciprocal disclosure raised trust and the depth of disclosure against a baseline bot. Whether persona drift contributes to bonding is unmeasured

cells.headline: The reply you react to, measured
cells.gloss: AI-written supportive replies made people feel more heard on average than untrained humans’ replies, and an AI label reduced that rating; in two preregistered trials, pre-generated AI replies elicited closeness in deep talk, especially when labelled human

cells.headline: Nobody meets a token; everyone meets its display
cells.gloss: A first-person hedge in an answer lowered reliance and raised accuracy for 404 people, at the grain of a phrase; no test reaches a single internal pass
